lost_facts.evidence: Shipped code (message index 189, transcript ~line 5533): MultiTurnAgenticProcessor._build_ledger(self, records, *, status: str = 'verified') — the ticket itself specifies build_ledger's default as status='verified' (ticket text, transcript line 85: 'status: str = "verified"'). In run() (message index 191, transcript ~line 5636), the very first ledger built after writing the seed line is `ledger = self._build_ledger(records)` — called with NO status override, so it silently takes the 'verified' default even though nothing has been verified (no sidecar existed yet, none was checked). 'created' is only ever passed explicitly inside load_ledger()'s internal call to build_ledger (`status='created'` immediately followed by verify_sidecar, which always rewrites it to 'adopted' or 'verified' before returning). The seed-write call site in run() needed the same explicit override and never got it. Contributing miss: g7.r1.l8 ('first write carries created, verified is only a load where both matched' — #pipeline 2025-03-24 18:30), the single clearest statement of this exact distinction, was never surfaced by any search in this run (grepped for its distinctive phrases, 0 hits). The agent's own reading of the two remarks it DID find on this topic (fix27, fix30) folded 'created' into load_ledger's internal machinery only (Analysis, line 4108: "verify_sidecar returns a ledger with an updated status: 'created' -> 'adopted'") rather than recognising it as a status a caller must persist for a truly-fresh, never-checked write.

search_strategy: The agent used three distinct, appropriate tools per surface and generally did not rely on BookStack free-text search alone for the wiki (which the world explicitly warns does not index comments): it fetched wiki pages whole via /api/pages/{id} (capturing body + comments together, e.g. lines 2180, 2280, 2523, 2558-2577, 2720-2726, 2055-2098), matching the 'a page worth reading is worth fetching whole' hint in the ticket. For Mattermost it combined full-text search (a custom script hitting the MM search API for terms like 'sentinel', 'COMPLETION_SENTINEL', 'turn_ledger') with direct channel-window dumps around dates surfaced by search hits (#pipeline 2025-03-17/03-19/03-24/05-13/06-13/12-30, #code-review 2025-01-21/01-22/03-14/03-18/04-24/04-25/06-04, #engineering, #incidents, #viewer, #cookbooks). For mail it used IMAP SEARCH/FETCH directly (subject and body term searches for 'sentinel', 'turn_ledger', 'interleave', 'seed', etc.) and read full threads by ID range into local files (/tmp/m1.txt..m3.txt), which is why long threads like l12/l16/l3/l7 were captured completely rather than as snippets. Two systematic gaps: (1) roughly a third of the 51 remarks were never surfaced at all (14 of 51, plus 2 herrings only seen secondhand through their reversals) — several of these were entire mail threads sent the SAME morning as threads that WERE read (e.g. g7.r1.l9 and g7.r2.g7r2-l08 are both 2025-04-09 08:12 threads; only the r2 one was opened), suggesting the mail search terms used did not enumerate every thread even when adjacent ones were found; (2) one wiki page (144, 'recovering an interrupted agent turn') was read in full but its BODY (elaborate, semi-fictional turn_ledger.jsonl/rematerialize scaffolding) was read while its planted COMMENT (the actual short remark carrying the real failure_behavior fact) was apparently never printed or quoted — the agent correctly flagged the page as 'possibly a decoy' and did not act on its scaffolding, which avoided a worse outcome but also meant the real comment underneath it was never used. Truncation (`| head`, chunked `sed -n` reads) shows up mechanically in the pointer sheet for g7.r2.g7r2-l07 but did not lose content there — the full comment thread was eventually printed across chunks.
notable: The two r1 facts that failed for the same underlying reason (failure_behavior, observability) both trace to one missing pair of attributes on TurnLedgerDesyncError, not two separate bugs — recorded_responses/recorded_last_author are used in the f-string message but never assigned as self attributes (transcript line ~5536, TurnLedgerDesyncError.__init__).

That missing-attribute decision was not a slip in the sense of contradicting the agent's own stated plan — it is exactly what the agent said it would do after reading g7.r1.l12's mail thread in full ('carrying .log_responses / .log_last_author ... settled in the June mail thread', line 8580). Per the coordinator, the v4 world this rollout ran against served an older version of that thread than the current answer key documents (a local edit to nikolai's reply was made 2026-09-10 and never pushed); the agent's implementation is a faithful read of what v4 actually contains, and the fact loss is a corpus/key version mismatch rather than a research failure.

The r1.scope loss (status 'created' vs 'verified') is a genuine implementation slip: the ticket's own default build_ledger(..., status: str = 'verified') is safe everywhere the agent used it except the one call site — the seed-line write inside run() — that specifically needed status='created'. The single remark that states this distinction most directly (g7.r1.l8, #pipeline 2025-03-24) was never found by any search in this run.

All four herring/reversal pairs were resolved correctly: in every case the agent's shipped code matches the later reversal, never the earlier herring, even though two of the four herrings (g7-h2-truncate-is-the-pattern, h2-sentinel-placement-free) were only ever seen secondhand as a quote embedded in their own reversal's text, not as an independently-read original exchange.

Wiki page 144 ('recovering-an-interrupted-agent-turn') is a well-disguised distractor: its body describes a plausible but non-canonical two-file (turn_ledger.json + turn_ledger.jsonl) repair architecture with a '.json.broken' backup scheme. The agent read it in full, explicitly called it 'possibly a decoy' (line 2038), and did not implement any of its rematerialize logic — a correct call that nonetheless meant the real planted comment on that same page (g7.r1.l11, carrying failure_behavior) was never surfaced or used.
